The cooperation with an experienced provider should achieve the following goals: * In the event of a disaster, Science IT receives professional support for OpenStack and CephFS on the next business day at the latest. * Employees will be able to benefit from the provider's expertise in the coming years. The provider also employs staff who are actively involved in CephFS and OpenStack as contributors. Using the provider's documentation on the UZH platform, the team will be enabled to solve problems independently. * Updates or upgrades can be planned and implemented together so that the platform is always operated at the second latest technical level. * Conceptual adjustments to the platform can be discussed with an experienced partner. title-proc.eng: Provision of technical services for the AIDRA project demonstration on AI-enabled on-board data processing

description-proc.eng: The European Union Satellite Centre (SatCen) seeks to award a direct service contract to support the implementation of AIDRA (Artificial Intelligence In-orbit Data pRocessing Assessment), a cooperative initiative between the SatCen and the European Defence Agency (EDA). AIDRA is designed as a proof-of-concept to assess the feasibility, traceability, operational implications and governance conditions of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enabled On-Board Data Processing (OBDP) in support of Earth Observation (EO) and Geospatial Intelligence (GEOINT) workflows. The purpose of AIDRA is to generate independent, evidence-based insights into the maturity, risks and potential benefits of AI-OBDP for GEOINT, in support of EU objectives on technological readiness, operational effectiveness and secure information governance. The objective of the demonstration is to evaluate, under space-representative conditions, how AI-enabled on-board processing and tasking functions perform within an end-to-end EO data chain. The assessment focuses on technical behaviour, system performance and interaction with existing GEOINT workflow requirements. The initiative does not aim to deploy an operational capability, but to generate structured evidence to support institutional evaluation.

title-proc.eng: Quality standard wild reindeer - data basis for Delnorm 1 Population performance

description-proc.eng: The Norwegian Environment Agency (the contracting authority) intends to enter into a one year individual agreement with Stiftelsen NINA for the collection of data basis for the quality standard for wild reindeer. The contract amount is estimated to NOK 3.0 million. The contract shall cover data collection on Lot 1 Population performance a-c for 2026, i.e. calf counts, structure counts and slaughter scales, in all wild reindeer areas. In 2026 data shall be collected, and this data shall be quality assured and processed to the degree necessary, in order to easily be used for the next classification, which we expect will be carried out in 2027. The division of responsibility for data collection was determined in connection with the first classification of wild reindeer areas in 2020. Work is being done in 2026 to put in place a more permanent organisation of the work on the quality norm where a secretariat is established, which can follow the data collection over time. The decision from 2020 means that the task will be solved by NINA, in cooperation with a number of actors. Consideration to the implementation with a consistent methodology is the reason why the contract will be concluded directly with NINA for 2026. The agreement shall include written documentation of the method. The aim is transparency about methodology, and to ensure relatively consistent methodology for counts over time. There will also be an important basic document for assessments and any testing of new methods for counting and for a future announcement of the secretariat function. The Norwegian Environment Agency plans to announce a procurement for a more long-term agreement for the secretariat function for quality norms for wild reindeer, which can also include following the data acquisition over time. This is an intention notice in accordance with the Public Procurement Regulations § 21-5 with a 10 day deadline calculated from the day after this notice has been published. The contracting authority will not enter into a contract until 11 days after publication at the earliest.

Safety is the overriding priority of this contract. The proposed inflatable park must demonstrate the highest standards of safe design, structural integrity, durability, stability and operational reliability, and must be fully suitable for intensive commercial use by children and families. The contract must include the complete inflatable unit, all blowers and associated equipment, anchoring or restraint systems as required, delivery, installation, commissioning, operating instructions, staff handover or training, warranty, and all relevant technical, safety and compliance documentation. Tenderers must demonstrate that the proposed inflatable park complies with the recognised safety standards and inspection requirements applicable to commercial inflatable play equipment. In particular, equipment should comply with BS EN 14960, which HSE identifies as the relevant standard for this type of inflatable play equipment. HSE also states that commercial play inflatables should display either a numbered PIPA tag or an ADiPs Declaration of Compliance to show compliance with BS EN 14960, together with written instructions for safe operation. Tenderers must therefore provide full details of compliance with BS EN 14960, together with all relevant inspection and safety documentation, including certification, operating manuals, maintenance requirements, supervision guidance, maximum user numbers, age/height restrictions where applicable, anchoring requirements, and emergency procedures. Full written instructions must be supplied for safe setup, operation, inspection, maintenance and shutdown. HSE guidance also notes that inflatables should not be used in winds above 24 mph / 38 km/h unless the manufacturer sets a lower limit, and safe use depends on proper anchoring, blower checks, pressure checks and written operating procedures. The successful tenderer must also demonstrate relevant experience in the manufacture and/or supply of commercial inflatable play equipment for public use and must provide details of warranty, aftersales support, spare parts availability, delivery timelines and installation arrangements. The airside buses will replace the complete existing bus fleet of 22 buses in an initial order, and the tender further has options to procure up to 18 additional buses.

title-proc.eng: MOST FOOTBRIDGE: New connection of the city, landscape and the lake

description-proc.ces: Předmětem soutěže o návrh je řešení nové pěší a cyklistické lávky, která překoná historicky vzniklou bariéru mezi městem Most a územím dnešního jezera Most, tvořenou souběhem silniční infrastruktury, železniční a tramvajové tratě a upraveného koryta řeky Bíliny. Cílem je nejen fyzické propojení obou částí města, ale také jejich symbolické a mentální znovusjednocení. Lávka se má stát klíčovým prvkem nové městské osy spojující centrum města, muzeum, rekreační oblast kolem jezera a lokalitu v okolí přesunutého kostela Nanebevzetí Panny Marie; zároveň se stane významnou architektonickou dominantou a novou vstupní branou do města při příjezdu od Litvínova. Součástí soutěžního zadání je rovněž návrh navazujících veřejných prostranství v předpolích lávky. Na straně města má vzniknout nový Muzejní park - důstojný předprostor muzea, který ve vzájemné synergii s kulturními institucemi a pamětními místy vytvoří kvalitní městský prostor s vysokou krajinnou, pobytovou a společenskou hodnotou. Na straně jezera mají soutěžní návrhy navrhnout krajinnou vazbu a pěší a cyklistické propojení mezi lávkou a jezerem Most a navrhnout přehledné a atraktivní nástupní místo do této oblasti. Řešené území je rozděleno na části. Předmětem navazující projektové fáze je řešení samotné lávky vč. předpolí a nový Muzejní park. V ideové rovině mají soutěžní návrhy prověřit možnost vzniku širšího liniového parku propojujícího muzeum a Státní okresní archiv a zároveň koncepci krajinného propojení směrem k jezeru Most. Cílem je vytvořit soudržný, čitelný a dlouhodobě udržitelný rámec pro postupnou transformaci tohoto klíčového území. Cílem soutěže je řešit území jako jeden celek a vybrat jeden multidisciplinární tým pro návrh lávky i parku. V odůvodněném případě však může porota rozhodnout o výběru dvou samostatných vítězů, což může vést k navazujícím samostatným Jednacím řízením bez uveřejnění (JŘBU) pro lávku a park.
description-proc.eng: The subject of the competition is a design for a new pedestrian and cycle bridge that will overcome the historically formed barrier between the town of Most and the new landscape of Lake Most, created by the convergence of road infrastructure, railway and tram lines, and the modified riverbed of the Bílina river. The aim is not only to physically connect the two parts of the city, but also to symbolically and mentally reunite them. The footbridge is set to become a key element of a new urban axis connecting the city centre, the museum, the recreational area around the lake and the site near the relocated Church of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary; at the same time, it will become a significant architectural landmark and a new gateway to the city when approaching from Litvínov. The competition brief also includes a proposal for the surrounding public spaces in front of the footbridge. On the town side, a new Museum Park is to be created – a dignified forecourt for the museum which, in synergy with cultural institutions and memorial sites, will form a high-quality urban space with significant landscape, recreational and social value. On the lake side, competition entries are to propose a landscape connection and pedestrian and cycle links between the footbridge and Lake Most, and to design a clear and attractive entry point to this area. The site is divided into sections. The subject of the subsequent tender is the complete project documentation of the footbridge itself, including the approach areas, and the new Museum Park. At a conceptual level, the competition entries should explore the possibility of creating a wider linear park connecting the Museum and also the State District Archives, as well as a concept for a landscape connection towards Lake Most. The aim is to create a coherent, clear and long-term sustainable framework for the gradual transformation of this key area.
